column1: # Original summaries of the local public-domain scripture. No publisher headings.
# chapter|title|summary

1-nephi-1|Lehi warns Jerusalem|Nephi begins his record with his father's visions. Lehi sees God and reads about Jerusalem's destruction. He warns the people and speaks of a Messiah. Some seek to kill him.

1-nephi-2|A family leaves Jerusalem|The Lord tells Lehi to leave Jerusalem. His family travels into the wilderness. Laman and Lemuel complain, but Nephi seeks God's help. The Lord promises Nephi a land if he obeys.

1-nephi-3|The search for the plates|Lehi sends his sons back for Laban's brass plates. Laban refuses their request and takes their property. Laman and Lemuel strike their younger brothers. An angel tells them to return.

1-nephi-4|Nephi brings back the records|Nephi enters Jerusalem and finds Laban drunk. The Spirit tells him to kill Laban. He takes the plates with help from Laban's servant, Zoram. Zoram agrees to join the family.

1-nephi-5|Sariah sees her sons return|Sariah fears that her sons have died. Their return strengthens her trust in the Lord. Lehi reads the brass plates and learns his family line. The family keeps the records for its journey.

1-nephi-6|Why Nephi writes|Nephi explains the purpose of his record. He leaves out his family's full genealogy. He wants readers to come to God and be saved. He tells later writers to preserve things of worth.

1-nephi-7|Ishmael's family joins the journey|Lehi sends his sons to bring Ishmael's family. Some rebel on the journey back. Nephi escapes the ropes that bind him. The families return to Lehi and give thanks.

1-nephi-8|Lehi's dream of the tree|Lehi describes a tree with desirable fruit. He invites his family to eat it. People follow an iron rod, lose their way, or mock others. Lehi urges Laman and Lemuel to obey the Lord.
1-nephi-9|Two sets of plates|Nephi describes two sets of records. One holds the history of kings and wars. The other gives more space to religious teaching. He trusts the Lord's purpose for both.

1-nephi-10|Lehi speaks of the Messiah|Lehi foretells Jerusalem's fall and the coming Messiah. He describes a prophet who will baptize the Messiah. He compares scattered Israel to broken olive branches. Nephi wants to learn these things for himself.

1-nephi-11|Nephi sees the Savior|The Spirit shows Nephi the tree from Lehi's dream. An angel shows him Mary and the Son of God. Nephi sees Christ's ministry, baptism, and death. He learns that the great building represents the world's pride.

1-nephi-12|Nephi sees his descendants|Nephi sees wars among his descendants. He sees destruction before Christ visits the survivors. Generations live in peace before pride and war return. His people's destruction follows.

1-nephi-13|Records cross the sea|Nephi sees nations beyond the promised land. He sees people cross the sea and receive a book. An angel describes truths lost from that record. Other records will make the Lamb's teachings known.

1-nephi-14|Two churches and a covenant|An angel describes the choices facing the Gentiles. He shows Nephi two opposing churches. God's covenant people receive power despite their small numbers. Nephi leaves part of the vision for another writer.

1-nephi-15|Nephi answers his brothers|Nephi finds his brothers disputing Lehi's words. He explains Israel's scattering and later gathering. He identifies the iron rod as God's word. He also explains the river and final judgment.

1-nephi-16|Hunger on the journey|The families marry and receive a guiding instrument. Nephi's broken bow leaves them without food. He makes another bow and asks where to hunt. Ishmael dies, and further complaints lead to the Lord's correction.

1-nephi-17|The command to build a ship|The family reaches a coast called Bountiful. The Lord tells Nephi to build a ship. His brothers mock him, and he recalls God's help to Moses. God's power shakes them when they oppose Nephi.

1-nephi-18|The voyage and the landing|The family finishes the ship and sails. Nephi's brothers bind him during the voyage. A storm ends after they release him. They reach the promised land and begin to plant crops.

1-nephi-19|Records and the suffering Savior|Nephi explains how he makes and uses his plates. He foretells the Savior's rejection and suffering. He recalls prophets who testified about Christ. He reads Isaiah to his brothers.

1-nephi-20|The Lord calls Israel to leave Babylon|Nephi quotes Isaiah's words to the house of Israel. The Lord rebukes false claims of faithfulness. He declares his power and purpose. He calls his people to leave Babylon.

1-nephi-21|The Lord remembers Zion|Isaiah describes a servant called to gather Israel. The Lord promises help to scattered people. Zion fears that the Lord has forgotten her. He promises to remember and rescue her children.

1-nephi-22|Nephi explains the gathering|Nephi explains Isaiah's words to his brothers. Israel will scatter and later receive God's help. The Lord will defeat those who fight his people. Nephi urges obedience and endurance.

2-nephi-1|Lehi's final counsel|Lehi recalls the Lord's help on the journey. He warns his sons about disobedience in the promised land. He asks them to support Nephi. He also blesses Zoram and his descendants.

2-nephi-2|Jacob hears about freedom and redemption|Lehi speaks to Jacob about suffering and redemption. He explains why opposition allows people to act. He describes Adam and Eve's choice. He urges his sons to choose life through the Messiah.

2-nephi-3|Lehi blesses Joseph|Lehi speaks to his youngest son, Joseph. He recalls Joseph of Egypt's promise about a future seer. Records from different peoples will join together. Lehi asks Joseph to follow Nephi's words.

2-nephi-4|Nephi's prayer after Lehi's death|Lehi blesses his descendants before he dies. Nephi recalls the Lord's goodness but grieves over his sins. He asks God to help him resist evil. His prayer ends with trust in God.

2-nephi-5|Nephi's people settle apart|Nephi leaves his brothers because they seek his life. His followers settle in a land they call Nephi. They build a temple and work the land. Nephi describes their records, worship, and later conflicts.

2-nephi-6|Jacob speaks about scattered Israel|Jacob teaches from Isaiah about Israel's future. He speaks of Jerusalem's loss and the Savior's rejection. Israel will gather when its people believe in Christ. The Lord will defend those who wait for him.

2-nephi-7|The servant trusts the Lord|Jacob quotes the Lord's questions about Israel's separation. A servant describes suffering without turning back. He trusts the Lord to defend him. The passage warns those who follow their own light.

2-nephi-8|Zion is called to awake|Isaiah asks the people to remember Abraham and Sarah. The Lord promises comfort and lasting salvation. Jerusalem must awake after suffering. Zion is called to rise from captivity.

2-nephi-9|Jacob explains resurrection and judgment|Jacob teaches that Christ rescues people from death. All will rise and face God's judgment. He warns against sins and pride in learning or wealth. He invites his hearers to turn to the Lord.

2-nephi-10|Jacob describes Israel's return|Jacob speaks again about Christ and Israel. He foretells Christ's rejection and the scattering of the Jews. The Lord promises their return when they believe. Jacob asks his hearers to choose God.

2-nephi-11|Nephi introduces Isaiah's words|Nephi records selected teachings from Jacob. He says that he, Jacob, and Isaiah have seen the Redeemer. He takes joy in God's promises and mercy. He introduces more words from Isaiah.

2-nephi-12|Nations come to the Lord's house|Isaiah sees nations coming to the Lord's house. He describes a future end to war. He then warns Judah about wealth, idols, and pride. The Lord's day will bring the proud low.

2-nephi-13|Judgment comes upon Jerusalem|Isaiah describes the loss of food and good rulers. The Lord judges leaders who take from the poor. Isaiah also condemns the pride of Zion's daughters. Jerusalem faces mourning and loss.

2-nephi-14|The Lord shelters the survivors|Isaiah describes survivors after Jerusalem's suffering. The Lord cleanses the city of blood and impurity. Those who remain in Zion are called holy. The Lord gives them shelter from heat and storms.

2-nephi-15|The vineyard bears bad fruit|Isaiah sings about a vineyard that bears bad fruit. The vineyard represents Israel and Judah. He condemns greed, drunkenness, and calling evil good. An invading people approaches the land.

2-nephi-16|Isaiah receives a call|Isaiah sees the Lord in the temple. A burning coal cleanses his lips. He accepts a call to speak to an unresponsive people. The vision also describes a remnant after destruction.

2-nephi-17|Isaiah speaks to Ahaz|Judah fears an attack from Syria and Israel. Isaiah tells Ahaz that their plan will fail. He gives the sign of Immanuel. He also warns about the coming power of Assyria.

2-nephi-18|Assyria threatens the land|Isaiah names a child as a sign of coming loss. Assyria will overwhelm Syria and Israel. The Lord warns against fear and false counsel. Isaiah looks to God's testimony while darkness spreads.

2-nephi-19|Light and judgment|Isaiah announces light for people in darkness. He describes a child who will rule with peace. The passage then turns to Israel's pride and injustice. God's judgment continues against the people.

2-nephi-20|Assyria's pride is judged|Isaiah condemns laws that harm the poor. Assyria serves as an instrument of judgment but boasts of its power. The Lord will punish that pride. A remnant of Israel will return.

2-nephi-21|A ruler and a gathered people|Isaiah describes a ruler from Jesse's family. He will judge fairly and defend the poor. Peace will reach even the animal world. The Lord will gather scattered Israel.

2-nephi-22|A song of thanks|Isaiah gives a song for the day of deliverance. The people thank the Lord for comfort. They praise him as their strength and salvation. They call others to make his deeds known.
2-nephi-23|Babylon faces destruction|Isaiah announces a judgment against Babylon. Armies gather for a day of terror. Babylon's pride and power will fall. The passage describes its lasting ruin.

2-nephi-24|The fall of a proud ruler|Isaiah promises rest for Israel. A song mocks the fallen king of Babylon. The Lord also announces judgment against Assyria. Philistia receives a warning about further danger.

2-nephi-25|Nephi explains his witness of Christ|Nephi explains why Isaiah can be hard to understand. He foretells Jerusalem's loss and the Jews' return. He testifies that salvation comes through Christ. He teaches his people to keep the law while looking to Christ.

2-nephi-26|Christ and the future of Nephi's people|Nephi foretells Christ's visit after signs and destruction. Pride will later destroy his people. He warns against churches built for gain. He teaches that God invites all people to receive his goodness.

2-nephi-27|A sealed book and a work of God|Nephi describes a future book and its sealed words. A learned man refuses to read the sealed record. The Lord gives his words to another reader. God promises a work that overturns human pride.

2-nephi-28|Warnings about false teaching|Nephi describes churches that dispute and teach false ideas. He warns against pride, easy excuses for sin, and spiritual sleep. The devil uses anger and false peace. God continues to teach those who receive his words.

2-nephi-29|The Lord speaks to more than one nation|The Lord answers those who reject additional scripture. He remembers the Jews and their record. He speaks to people in many nations. Their records will come together.

2-nephi-30|Scattered peoples receive the gospel|Nephi describes people receiving the record and believing in Christ. Descendants of his people will learn their history. Jews and Gentiles will join God's covenant through repentance. The passage looks toward peace and revealed truth.

2-nephi-31|Nephi teaches the path of Christ|Nephi recalls the Savior's baptism. He teaches repentance, baptism, and receiving the Holy Ghost. These acts begin the path toward eternal life. Followers must continue with faith, hope, and love.

2-nephi-32|Words of Christ and prayer|Nephi answers questions about what follows baptism. Christ's words tell believers what to do. The Spirit will also guide them. Nephi tells them to pray before they act.

2-nephi-33|Nephi closes his record|Nephi explains his care for his people. He trusts God to make his written words useful. He asks readers to believe in Christ. He ends with a warning to those who reject his words.

jacob-1|Jacob receives the small plates|Nephi gives Jacob charge of the small plates. Jacob must preserve important religious teachings. A new king rules after Nephi's death. Jacob and Joseph teach against growing sins.

jacob-2|Jacob condemns pride and unfaithfulness|Jacob speaks with grief about his people's sins. He condemns pride in wealth and mistreatment of others. He then rebukes unauthorized plural marriages. He describes the pain caused to wives and children.

jacob-3|Jacob addresses the pure in heart|Jacob asks the pure in heart to trust God. He warns the unrepentant Nephites of destruction. He praises the Lamanites' faithfulness to their families. He tells the Nephites to remember their own sins.

jacob-4|Jacob writes about faith in Christ|Jacob explains why his people preserve records. He describes prophets who trusted Christ before his coming. He asks readers to receive God's counsel. He introduces a question about Israel's rejected foundation.

jacob-5|Zenos's story of the olive trees|Jacob quotes Zenos's account of a vineyard. Its lord and servants tend, prune, and graft olive trees. Good fruit later becomes corrupt. A final effort preserves good fruit before the vineyard's end.

jacob-6|Jacob explains the vineyard's warning|Jacob applies Zenos's words to his hearers. God will again work to gather Israel. Jacob asks the people to repent while mercy is offered. He warns of judgment and ends his teaching.

jacob-7|Sherem challenges Jacob|Sherem denies that Christ will come. Jacob defends his witness and refuses to seek a sign. Sherem receives a sign, confesses, and dies. Jacob later gives the plates to Enos.

enos-1|Enos prays for his people|Enos prays and receives forgiveness for his sins. He then prays for the Nephites and Lamanites. The Lord promises to preserve the records. Enos describes his ministry and hope in the Redeemer.

jarom-1|A people preserved through warning|Jarom writes briefly about the Nephites. Prophets call them to repentance and faith in the coming Messiah. They defend themselves against repeated attacks. Jarom gives the plates to Omni.

omni-1|Records reach Benjamin|Several writers briefly preserve the family record. Amaleki tells how Mosiah's people reach Zarahemla. They join the people already living there. Amaleki gives the plates to Benjamin and invites readers to Christ.

words-of-mormon-1|Mormon joins the records|Mormon describes finding Nephi's small plates. He joins them to his larger record. He recalls Benjamin's battles and the work of prophets. Their efforts restore peace among the people.

mosiah-1|Benjamin prepares his sons|Benjamin teaches his sons from the preserved records. He explains why those records matter. He appoints Mosiah to succeed him. Mosiah calls the people together to hear Benjamin.

mosiah-2|Benjamin speaks about service|Benjamin addresses families gathered near the temple. He recalls serving them without seeking wealth. He teaches that service to others serves God. He warns against rebellion and urges obedience.

mosiah-3|An angel's message about Christ|Benjamin recounts an angel's message. Jesus Christ will suffer, die, and rise. His sacrifice offers salvation to those who repent. Benjamin teaches humility and warns of judgment.

mosiah-4|Forgiveness and care for the poor|The people ask for mercy and receive forgiveness. Benjamin teaches them to remember God's greatness and goodness. He asks them to teach their children and help the poor. He warns them to watch their thoughts, words, and deeds.

mosiah-5|The people make a covenant|The people say that Benjamin's words have changed their hearts. They covenant to obey God. Benjamin calls them children of Christ. He asks them to remain faithful to the name they have received.

mosiah-6|Mosiah begins to rule|Benjamin records the names of those who made the covenant. He appoints priests and makes Mosiah king. Benjamin later dies. Mosiah works the land and seeks his people's peace.

mosiah-7|Ammon finds Limhi's people|Mosiah sends men to search for Zeniff's people. Ammon reaches Shilom and meets King Limhi. Limhi learns that Zarahemla still exists. He calls his people together and urges them to trust God.

mosiah-8|Limhi asks about the unknown records|Ammon teaches Limhi's people. Limhi describes a search party that found ruins and metal plates. He asks whether someone can read them. Ammon explains the work of a seer.

mosiah-9|Zeniff returns to Nephi|Zeniff recalls his desire to settle in Nephi. King Laman gives his people Nephi and Shilom. They rebuild and farm the land. They later defend themselves against a Lamanite attack.

mosiah-10|Zeniff defends his people|Zeniff prepares weapons and guards. A Lamanite army attacks after years of peace. He describes the beliefs that drive their hatred. His people prevail, and he later gives the kingdom to a son.

mosiah-11|Noah rejects Abinadi's warning|Noah rules with heavy taxes and corrupt priests. He builds richly while his people become wicked. Abinadi warns that bondage will follow unless they repent. Noah and the people reject him.

mosiah-12|Abinadi answers the priests|Abinadi returns and warns again of judgment. The people take him to Noah. The priests question him about Isaiah. He challenges their conduct and teaching of God's commandments.

mosiah-13|Abinadi teaches the commandments|Noah orders Abinadi's death, but God's power protects him. Abinadi continues to teach the commandments. He says the law alone cannot save people. He points to the coming Redeemer.

mosiah-14|Isaiah's suffering servant|Abinadi quotes Isaiah's account of a suffering servant. The servant bears others' grief and sins. He suffers without answering his accusers. His death and offering benefit many.

mosiah-15|Abinadi explains Christ's redemption|Abinadi teaches that God will come to redeem his people. He describes Christ's suffering and victory over death. He identifies those who receive the first resurrection. He also speaks of messengers who publish peace.

mosiah-16|Resurrection and the final judgment|Abinadi warns that all people will face God. He explains how Christ overcomes death. People will rise to receive judgment for their works. He asks the priests to teach redemption through Christ.

mosiah-17|Abinadi dies and Alma believes|Alma believes Abinadi and asks Noah to release him. Noah sends servants to kill Alma. Abinadi refuses to withdraw his testimony. He dies by fire after warning his killers.

mosiah-18|Alma gathers believers at Mormon|Alma secretly teaches Abinadi's words. Believers gather at the waters of Mormon and receive baptism. Alma organizes priests and teaches unity and care for others. The group flees after Noah discovers them.

mosiah-19|Noah falls and Limhi rules|Gideon opposes Noah as a Lamanite army arrives. Noah flees, leaving many families behind. His people later kill him by fire. Limhi becomes king under a tribute agreement.

mosiah-20|An abduction brings another attack|Noah's priests take Lamanite daughters from Shemlon. The Lamanites blame Limhi's people and attack. Limhi learns the cause and spares their wounded king. The king returns with them and restores peace.

mosiah-21|Limhi's people seek deliverance|Limhi's people suffer under Lamanite control. Repeated attempts to fight free fail. They humble themselves and receive some relief. Ammon's arrival gives them hope of escape.

mosiah-22|Limhi's people escape|Limhi and Ammon seek a way out of bondage. Gideon proposes getting the guards drunk. The people leave with their families, flocks, and records. They reach Zarahemla while their pursuers become lost.

mosiah-23|Alma's people settle in Helam|Alma's people flee and settle in Helam. Alma refuses to become their king. A lost Lamanite army finds them and Noah's former priests. Amulon gains authority over Alma's people.

mosiah-24|Alma's people leave bondage|Amulon burdens Alma's people and forbids their prayers. They pray silently, and the Lord strengthens them. The Lord causes their guards to sleep. They escape through the wilderness and reach Zarahemla.

mosiah-25|The communities join in Zarahemla|Mosiah gathers the people and reads the records of the returning groups. The people grieve and rejoice at what they hear. Alma teaches and baptizes Limhi's people. Churches are organized throughout the land.

mosiah-26|Alma seeks guidance about sin|Some younger people reject the church's teachings. Alma brings their cases to Mosiah, who returns them. Alma prays and receives instructions from the Lord. He teaches repentance and removes those who refuse it.

mosiah-27|Alma and Mosiah's sons change|Alma and Mosiah's sons work against the church. An angel stops them and calls Alma to repent. Alma recovers after the people pray and describes his change. The men begin to repair the harm they caused.

mosiah-28|Mosiah's sons ask to preach|Mosiah's sons ask to teach the Lamanites. The Lord tells Mosiah to let them go. Mosiah translates the records found by Limhi's people. He gives Alma charge of the sacred records.

mosiah-29|Judges replace the kings|Mosiah explains the dangers of rule by a wicked king. He proposes judges chosen by the people. The people accept, and Alma becomes chief judge. Mosiah and the elder Alma die.

alma-1|Nehor's teaching and trial|Nehor teaches for gain and kills Gideon. Alma judges him under the law. Persecution continues after Nehor's death. Church members share their goods and care for the poor.

alma-2|Amlici's rebellion reaches the Sidon|The people reject Amlici's bid to become king. His followers rebel and join a Lamanite army. Alma leads the Nephites through battles near Zarahemla and the Sidon. The enemy retreats into Hermounts.

alma-3|The cost of rebellion|The Nephites bury their dead after the battles. The record describes the Amlicites' identifying marks. Another Lamanite attack follows. The chapter closes by linking each person's choices to their reward.

alma-4|Alma leaves the judgment seat|War leads many people to humble themselves. Later wealth brings pride and neglect of the poor. Alma sees that the church needs correction. He gives Nephihah the judgment seat so he can preach.

alma-5|Alma asks about changed hearts|Alma reminds Zarahemla's people of their fathers' deliverance. He asks whether their hearts have changed. He warns against pride, envy, and mistreatment of others. He calls both church members and others to repentance.

alma-6|Alma goes to Gideon|Alma puts the church in Zarahemla in order. Those who repent receive baptism. The people meet, fast, and pray for those outside the church. Alma crosses the Sidon to teach in Gideon.

alma-7|Alma teaches Gideon about Christ|Alma speaks to the people in Gideon. He foretells Christ's birth and suffering for his people. He asks them to repent and receive baptism. He urges faith, hope, charity, and care for God's commandments.
alma-8|Alma meets Amulek|Alma teaches in Melek and then goes north to Ammonihah. The people reject him. An angel sends him back, and Amulek welcomes him. The two men prepare to preach together.

alma-9|Alma warns Ammonihah|The people challenge Alma's authority and words. He recalls the Lord's help to their ancestors. Their knowledge makes their rejection especially serious. He warns of destruction and the coming Son of God.

alma-10|Amulek gives his witness|Amulek tells how an angel led him to welcome Alma. He confirms Alma's words. Lawyers try to trap him through questions. He warns that the prayers of the righteous preserve the city.

alma-11|Amulek answers Zeezrom|The record explains the judges' pay and money system. Zeezrom offers Amulek money to deny God. Amulek refuses and teaches about Christ. He explains resurrection and judgment.

alma-12|Alma explains judgment and redemption|Alma exposes the purpose of Zeezrom's questions. He teaches about softened and hardened hearts. He describes judgment and the fall of Adam. He asks the people to repent and enter God's rest.

alma-13|Priests teach the way to God's rest|Alma explains the calling of priests. Their teaching points people toward the Son of God. He recalls Melchizedek's work among a people who repented. He urges his hearers to repent before the Lord comes.

alma-14|Believers suffer and the prison falls|The people cast out believing men and burn women, children, and scriptures. Alma and Amulek witness the deaths and suffer in prison. They pray for strength. The prison falls, and they escape.

alma-15|Zeezrom is healed in Sidom|Alma and Amulek find refugees in Sidom. Zeezrom asks for healing and expresses faith in Christ. Alma heals him, and he receives baptism. Alma establishes the church and later takes Amulek home.

alma-16|Ammonihah falls and captives return|Lamanites destroy Ammonihah and take captives from nearby lands. Alma tells Zoram where to find the enemy. The army recovers the captives near the Sidon. Alma and Amulek continue to teach throughout the land.

alma-17|Ammon serves in Ishmael|Alma meets Mosiah's sons after their mission. The account returns to their journey among the Lamanites. Ammon becomes a servant of King Lamoni. He protects the king's flocks from attackers.

alma-18|Lamoni hears Ammon's teaching|Lamoni hears what Ammon did for his servants. He wonders whether Ammon is the Great Spirit. Ammon teaches him about God, creation, and redemption. Lamoni prays for mercy and falls to the earth.

alma-19|Lamoni's household awakens|Lamoni's wife asks Ammon about her husband. Lamoni awakens and testifies of the Redeemer. His household experiences God's power, and Abish gathers the people. Many believe and receive baptism.

alma-20|Ammon helps free his brothers|Ammon and Lamoni travel toward Middoni to release Ammon's companions. They meet Lamoni's father, who commands his son to kill Ammon. Ammon resists the king and spares his life. The king permits his son's freedom and the prisoners' release.

alma-21|Aaron teaches and suffers imprisonment|Aaron teaches in Jerusalem and then Ani-Anti. Many reject his words. He and his companions suffer in prison in Middoni. After their release, they continue teaching while Ammon serves Lamoni's people.

alma-22|Aaron teaches the king; Mormon describes the lands|Aaron teaches Lamoni's father about God and redemption. The king prays and falls to the earth. Aaron raises him, and the household believes. Mormon then describes the lands, seas, wilderness, and narrow neck.

alma-23|Converted communities take a new name|The king protects the missionaries throughout his lands. Many Lamanites believe and give up rebellion. The record names communities that accept the teaching. The converts take the name Anti-Nephi-Lehies.

alma-24|The people bury their weapons|Enemies prepare to attack the converted Lamanites. Their king asks them to keep their promise against killing. They bury their weapons and refuse to fight. Many attackers repent after killing people who offer no resistance.

alma-25|War and further conversions|Lamanite armies attack the Nephites and destroy Ammonihah. Some descendants of Noah's priests suffer death. Many Lamanites later join the Anti-Nephi-Lehies. Mosiah's sons rejoice in the mission's results.

alma-26|Ammon gives thanks for the mission|Ammon recalls the missionaries' hardships and the many converts. Aaron warns him against boasting. Ammon gives the credit to God's strength and mercy. He rejoices that God remembers every people.

alma-27|The people of Ammon receive Jershon|Renewed attacks threaten the Anti-Nephi-Lehies. Ammon asks the Lord whether they should leave. The Nephites give them Jershon and provide protection. They become known as the people of Ammon.

alma-28|Loss and hope after battle|A great battle follows the settlement in Jershon. Many families mourn their dead. Some grieve without hope, while others trust God's promises. The record recalls the missionaries' work and its results.

alma-29|Alma rejoices in the work given to him|Alma wishes he could speak with an angel's power. He then accepts the work God has given him. He rejoices in the repentance of others. He also celebrates his companions' success among the Lamanites.

alma-30|Korihor challenges belief in Christ|Korihor teaches that there will be no Christ. Leaders bring him before Alma. He demands a sign and loses his ability to speak. He confesses his deception and later dies among the Zoramites.

alma-31|Alma sees the Zoramites' worship|Alma leads companions to Antionum. They see the Zoramites repeat a prayer from a high stand. The prayer rejects Christ and claims special favor. Alma prays for strength and for the people's return.

alma-32|Alma compares faith to a seed|Poor Zoramites seek help after being excluded from their worship places. Alma teaches them about humility and faith. He asks them to test the word like a planted seed. Patient care can bring its fruit.

alma-33|Prayer and belief in the Son|The people ask how to worship and exercise faith. Alma recalls Zenos's prayers outside worship buildings. He cites prophets who testified of God's Son. He asks them to believe and nourish that word.

alma-34|Amulek teaches redemption and daily prayer|Amulek teaches that Christ's sacrifice brings redemption. He asks the people to pray in daily life. Prayer must go with care for those in need. He warns them against delaying repentance.

alma-35|The believers leave Antionum|The Zoramites expel those who believe the missionaries. The people of Ammon welcome them in Jershon. Threats follow, and the people of Ammon move to Melek. Alma gathers his sons to give each one counsel.

alma-36|Alma tells Helaman about his change|Alma asks Helaman to remember God's deliverance. He recalls his rebellion and the angel's visit. Calling on Jesus brings relief from his anguish. He spends his later life teaching others.

alma-37|Helaman receives the sacred records|Alma gives Helaman charge of the records. He explains how small means can accomplish great things. He warns against sharing the secret acts in the Jaredite record. He compares Christ's guidance to the family's guiding instrument.

alma-38|Alma counsels Shiblon|Alma praises Shiblon's faithfulness during the mission. He recalls his own deliverance through Christ. He tells Shiblon to avoid pride and control his desires. He sends him back to teach the people.

alma-39|Alma corrects Corianton|Alma rebukes Corianton for abandoning his mission and pursuing Isabel. His conduct has harmed the Zoramites' response to the teaching. Alma tells him to repent and repair his wrongs. He explains why they proclaim Christ before his coming.

alma-40|Alma answers questions about resurrection|Alma addresses Corianton's concern about the dead. He distinguishes the state of spirits from resurrection. God's power will reunite body and spirit. All will face judgment after they rise.

alma-41|Restoration follows people's choices|Alma explains restoration to Corianton. Resurrection restores the body, and judgment answers people's works and desires. Restoration does not turn wickedness into happiness. Alma urges mercy, justice, and good conduct.

alma-42|Alma explains justice and mercy|Corianton questions the punishment of sinners. Alma explains the fall, human choice, and repentance. Christ's sacrifice allows mercy without removing justice. Alma asks his son to repent and return to teaching.

alma-43|Moroni prepares an ambush near Manti|Zerahemnah leads an army against the Nephites. Moroni's defenses cause the enemy to leave Antionum for Manti. He places troops on both sides of the Sidon. The Nephites surround the enemy, and Moroni stops the killing.

alma-44|Moroni offers terms to Zerahemnah|Moroni asks the enemy to surrender its weapons and promise peace. Zerahemnah refuses the promise. Fighting resumes after he attacks Moroni. The survivors finally accept the terms and leave.

alma-45|Helaman receives counsel and teaches|Alma asks Helaman about his faith. He foretells the future destruction of the Nephites. Alma leaves and is not seen again. Helaman and his companions organize churches as pride spreads.

alma-46|Moroni opposes Amalickiah|Amalickiah seeks power with support from dissenters. Moroni raises a written pledge of freedom and faith. The people covenant to defend those commitments. Amalickiah escapes while many of his followers return.

alma-47|Amalickiah takes the Lamanite throne|Amalickiah uses deception to control a Lamanite army. He arranges Lehonti's death. His servants kill the king and blame others. He marries the queen and becomes king.

alma-48|Preparations for another war|Amalickiah stirs the Lamanites against the Nephites. Moroni strengthens cities and places defenses at weak points. Mormon describes Moroni's faith and care for freedom. The Nephites prepare for war despite their desire for peace.

alma-49|The defenses hold at Ammonihah and Noah|Lamanite armies find Ammonihah strongly defended. They turn to Noah and find defenses there too. Their attack fails with heavy losses. The Nephites give thanks and enjoy peace.

alma-50|New defenses and Morianton's flight|Moroni strengthens the frontier and establishes eastern cities. Lehi and Morianton's people dispute land. Morianton leads his people toward the land northward. Teancum stops them at the narrow pass, and Pahoran later becomes chief judge.

alma-51|Division and an attack along the east coast|A dispute over kings divides the Nephites. Moroni suppresses the king-men as Amalickiah attacks eastern cities. The army reaches the borders near Bountiful. Teancum enters its camp and kills Amalickiah.

alma-52|The Nephites retake Mulek|Ammoron succeeds Amalickiah and continues the war. Moroni and Teancum plan to draw troops out of Mulek. Teancum retreats toward Bountiful while other troops take the city. The pursuing Lamanites are surrounded and captured.

alma-53|Helaman leads young men to war|Prisoners work on defenses near Bountiful. Trouble continues on the western front. The people of Ammon consider breaking their promise against fighting. Their sons enlist instead, with Helaman as leader.

alma-54|Letters about the prisoners|Ammoron proposes an exchange of prisoners. Moroni asks for Nephite families as well as soldiers. He demands that the invaders leave the land. Ammoron accepts the exchange terms but rejects Moroni's demands for peace.

alma-55|Moroni frees prisoners at Gid|Moroni refuses to proceed with the exchange. He sends wine to the guards at Gid through a Lamanite servant. The prisoners receive weapons while the guards sleep. The Nephites take the city without killing the guards.

alma-56|Helaman reports the battle near Antiparah|Helaman writes to Moroni about the western war. His young soldiers join Antipus at Judea. They draw the enemy away from Antiparah. They fight after Antipus falls, and all Helaman's young men survive.

alma-57|Cumeni falls and the young soldiers stand|Helaman's army receives reinforcements and takes Cumeni. A large group of prisoners attempts to escape. Lamanites attack the Nephites while part of the army is away. Helaman's young soldiers hold firm, and none of them dies.

alma-58|Helaman retakes Manti|Helaman's army waits for supplies and men. They pray for strength and receive assurance. Gid and Teomner take Manti while Helaman draws its army away. Helaman ends his letter with concern about limited government support.

alma-59|Nephihah falls before help arrives|Moroni rejoices at Helaman's letter and asks for help. A growing Lamanite force attacks Nephihah. The city falls, and survivors flee to Moroni. He fears that the government has failed his armies.

alma-60|Moroni sends a sharp letter|Moroni accuses Pahoran and the government of neglecting the armies. He recalls the soldiers who have died without help. He demands supplies and troops. He threatens action if the government continues to refuse.

alma-61|Pahoran explains the rebellion|Pahoran tells Moroni that rebels have driven him from Zarahemla. He is gathering supporters in Gideon. He accepts Moroni's concern without anger. He asks Moroni to come and help restore the government.

alma-62|The government returns and the war ends|Moroni joins Pahoran and defeats the rebels in Zarahemla. The Nephites retake Nephihah and other eastern cities. Teancum kills Ammoron but dies during the attempt. Peace returns, and Helaman teaches until his death.

alma-63|Ships, migration, and the records|Shiblon receives the records after Helaman's death. Many people move to the land northward. Hagoth builds ships by the west sea. Shiblon later gives the records to Helaman's son, Helaman.

helaman-1|A divided government leaves Zarahemla exposed|Pahoran's sons compete for the judgment seat. Kishkumen murders the chosen ruler. Coriantumr leads a Lamanite army into Zarahemla. Moronihah and Lehi surround the invaders and retake the city.

helaman-2|A plot against Helaman fails|Helaman becomes chief judge. Kishkumen plots to kill him with support from Gadianton. Helaman's servant discovers the plan and kills Kishkumen. Gadianton's group escapes into the wilderness.

helaman-3|People move north and the church grows|Many people settle in the land northward. The record describes their building materials and records. The church gains many members during years of peace. Pride returns, and Nephi later succeeds Helaman as chief judge.

helaman-4|The Nephites lose the land southward|Dissenters join the Lamanites in renewed war. The Nephites retreat to Bountiful and fortify a line. Moronihah recovers some land as prophets call the people to repent. The people recognize that their own sins have weakened them.

helaman-5|Nephi and Lehi teach among the Lamanites|Nephi leaves the judgment seat to preach with Lehi. They travel from Bountiful through Gid, Mulek, Zarahemla, and Nephi. God's power protects them in prison. Many Lamanites believe and return occupied lands.

helaman-6|Peace gives way to secret violence|Lamanites and Nephites trade and travel in peace. Many Lamanites teach the Nephites. Murders and secret agreements then spread among the Nephites. The Lamanites oppose the robbers while Nephite leaders support them.

helaman-7|Nephi mourns over Zarahemla|Nephi returns and finds corrupt leaders in power. He prays on his garden tower. A crowd gathers, and he calls them to repentance. He warns that rejection of God will bring destruction.

helaman-8|Nephi announces the chief judge's murder|Corrupt judges challenge Nephi's warning. He recalls prophets who testified of Christ. He tells the crowd that their chief judge has been murdered. He identifies the judge's brother as the killer.

helaman-9|The murderer's confession confirms Nephi's words|Men find the chief judge dead and are accused of murder. Nephi is also accused. He tells the judges how to question Seantum. Seantum confesses, leaving the people divided about Nephi.

helaman-10|Nephi receives power and returns to preach|Nephi walks home after the murder inquiry. The Lord praises his faithfulness and gives him sealing power. He returns to warn the people. They resist, and conflict increases.

helaman-11|Famine interrupts the war|Nephi asks for famine to stop the people's fighting. Hunger leads them to repent and remove the robbers. He prays for rain, and the land recovers. Prosperity later gives way to new robber bands and growing pride.

helaman-12|Mormon reflects on human forgetfulness|Mormon compares human pride with creation's obedience to God. People often forget the Lord when they prosper. The earth and its elements obey his command. Mormon closes with repentance, grace, and final judgment.

helaman-13|Samuel warns from the city wall|Samuel is rejected but returns to speak from Zarahemla's wall. He warns of destruction unless the people repent. He condemns their love of riches and rejection of prophets. He asks them to seek mercy before it is too late.

helaman-14|Samuel gives signs of Christ's birth and death|Samuel announces signs of Christ's birth in five years. He describes darkness and destruction at Christ's death. He teaches that Christ's death makes resurrection possible. He urges the people to choose repentance and life.

helaman-15|Samuel contrasts two peoples' choices|Samuel warns the Nephites about their knowledge and rebellion. He describes Lamanites who now keep God's commandments. Their faith has led them to bury their weapons. He warns that unrepentant Nephites will face destruction.

helaman-16|People accept or reject Samuel's warning|Some listeners seek baptism from Nephi. Others try to kill Samuel, who escapes. Signs and wonders increase. Many explain them away and continue in unbelief.

3-nephi-1|The sign of Christ's birth|Unbelievers threaten those waiting for Samuel's promised sign. Nephi prays, and the Lord promises that the sign will come. A night without darkness confirms Christ's birth. Belief spreads, but later dissent weakens some families.

3-nephi-2|Unbelief returns and war spreads|The people begin to forget the signs. They count their years from Christ's birth. Robber bands threaten both Nephites and Lamanites. The two peoples join in defense, but divisions continue.

3-nephi-3|Lachoneus gathers the people|Giddianhi demands that Lachoneus surrender to the robbers. Lachoneus refuses and gathers his people with supplies and flocks. Gidgiddoni prepares defenses between Zarahemla and Bountiful. The people repent and prepare to withstand an attack.

3-nephi-4|The gathered people defeat the robbers|The robbers find the abandoned lands without food. Giddianhi attacks the gathered people and dies. Zemnarihah tries a siege and later retreats. The defenders capture him and give thanks for their deliverance.

3-nephi-5|Mormon explains his record and purpose|The people repent after the robbers' defeat. Prisoners receive a chance to leave their former ways. Mormon explains his work in preserving the records. He looks toward Israel's gathering through Jesus Christ.

3-nephi-6|Peace breaks under pride and secret plots|The people return to their lands and rebuild. Wealth and rank divide them. Some judges secretly kill people who testify of Christ. Their allies plot to destroy the governor and establish a king.

3-nephi-7|The government falls into tribal rule|The governor's murder destroys the central government. Families divide into tribes. Jacob leads a secret group northward and becomes its king. Nephi teaches with power, and many receive baptism.

3-nephi-8|Storm, destruction, and darkness|The people await the sign of Christ's death. A great storm destroys cities, roads, and land. Zarahemla burns, Moroni sinks, and earth covers Moronihah. Darkness follows, and survivors mourn their refusal to repent.

3-nephi-9|Christ calls the survivors to return|A voice names cities destroyed for their wickedness. The speaker identifies himself as Jesus Christ. He invites the survivors to come to him and receive healing. He asks for a broken heart and a repentant spirit.

3-nephi-10|The darkness ends|Silence follows Christ's words. He calls the people to gather as children under his protection. The darkness lifts and the earth becomes still. Mormon prepares to describe the Savior's ministry to the survivors.

3-nephi-11|Jesus appears at Bountiful|People gather near the temple in Bountiful. The Father introduces his Son, and Jesus descends. The people touch his wounds and witness his resurrection. He calls disciples and teaches baptism without dispute.

3-nephi-12|Jesus teaches his people how to live|Jesus blesses those who receive his disciples and believe. He teaches about humility, mercy, and peace. He calls the people to reject anger and unfaithfulness. He asks them to love their enemies and follow God's example.

3-nephi-13|Jesus teaches private worship and trust|Jesus warns against giving, praying, or fasting to gain praise. He gives a pattern for prayer. He teaches forgiveness and treasure in heaven. He asks his chosen disciples to trust the Father's care.

3-nephi-14|Jesus teaches judgment and a firm foundation|Jesus warns against judging others while ignoring one's own faults. He tells the people to ask God and treat others well. He warns about false prophets. He compares obedient hearers to a house built on rock.

3-nephi-15|Jesus explains the law and his other sheep|Jesus says that he has fulfilled the law of Moses. God's remaining promises will still be fulfilled. He identifies this people as other sheep he mentioned in Jerusalem. They have heard his voice and belong to his flock.

3-nephi-16|Other peoples and Israel's gathering|Jesus speaks of still other sheep who will hear him. He describes the Gentiles receiving his gospel. He warns that unbelief can cost them that blessing. He promises to remember his covenant with Israel.

3-nephi-17|Jesus heals and blesses the children|Jesus tells the people to ponder and prepare for more teaching. Seeing their desire, he stays to heal the sick. He prays for them and blesses their children. Angels gather around the children in fire.

3-nephi-18|Bread, wine, and prayer|Jesus gives the people bread and wine. He teaches them to remember him and obey his commandments. He tells them to pray together and welcome others. He gives further instructions to the disciples before departing.

3-nephi-19|The people pray as Jesus returns|The people gather again with the twelve disciples. The disciples teach, baptize, and pray for the Holy Ghost. Jesus returns and prays to the Father. He rejoices in the people's faith.

3-nephi-20|Jesus speaks about the covenant with Israel|Jesus again gives the people bread and wine. He teaches about Israel's gathering and the promised land. He identifies them as children of the covenant. He quotes promises about Jerusalem's redemption.

3-nephi-21|A record becomes a sign of gathering|Jesus gives a sign of Israel's coming gathering. His words will reach the descendants of this people through the Gentiles. He warns the unrepentant and promises help to believers. He describes a New Jerusalem and God's work among all nations.

3-nephi-22|The Lord promises peace to his people|Jesus quotes Isaiah's promise to a once-desolate people. They are told to enlarge their tent for returning children. The Lord promises lasting kindness and a covenant of peace. He promises protection against their enemies.

3-nephi-23|Jesus asks that the records be complete|Jesus commands the people to study Isaiah. He examines their records with Nephi. Samuel's prophecy about resurrected people had not been recorded. Jesus tells them to add it and teaches from the scriptures.

3-nephi-24|Malachi's words about return and judgment|Jesus gives the people words from Malachi. The Lord will come and cleanse his servants. He calls the people to return and bring their tithes. A record preserves those who fear and remember him.

3-nephi-25|Malachi's words about the coming day|Jesus continues Malachi's words. A coming day will burn up the wicked. Those who fear the Lord will receive healing. Elijah will come to turn the hearts of parents and children.

3-nephi-26|Teaching continues beyond the written account|Jesus explains the scriptures and events from beginning to end. Mormon includes only part of that teaching. Children speak remarkable things after Jesus teaches them. The disciples baptize, and the people share their goods.

3-nephi-27|Jesus names his church and teaches his gospel|The disciples ask Jesus what to call the church. He tells them to use his name. He teaches his death, resurrection, repentance, and judgment. He asks them to follow his example and keep records.

3-nephi-28|Three disciples ask to continue their ministry|Jesus asks the disciples what they desire. Nine ask to come to him after their lives. Three ask to remain and bring people to him. Mormon describes their changed condition and protected ministry.

3-nephi-29|Mormon warns future readers|Mormon addresses those who will receive the record. Its arrival shows that the Lord remembers his covenant. He warns against rejecting Christ and his gifts. He also warns against mistreating Israel.

3-nephi-30|A call to the Gentiles|Mormon records Christ's words to the Gentiles. They must turn from their sins and repent. Christ calls them to receive baptism and the Holy Ghost. They can then be numbered with his people.

4-nephi-1|Unity gives way to division|The people live together in faith after Christ's visit. They share their goods and have no disputes. Later pride, separate churches, and old divisions return. Ammaron hides the sacred records as wickedness spreads.

mormon-1|Mormon's childhood and the coming war|Ammaron tells young Mormon where to find the records. Mormon travels with his father to Zarahemla. War begins near the Sidon. Mormon knows the Lord but cannot teach a people who reject repentance.

mormon-2|Mormon leads a people in retreat|Mormon becomes commander while still young. His army loses cities and retreats through Joshua, Jashon, and Shem. Their sorrow does not lead to true repentance. A treaty gives the Nephites the land northward.

mormon-3|Mormon refuses a war of revenge|Mormon strengthens defenses at Desolation and the narrow pass. The Nephites repel attacks but boast and vow revenge. Mormon refuses to lead them in that purpose. He turns to warning the future readers of his record.

mormon-4|The Nephites lose Desolation and Boaz|The Nephites attack the Lamanites and are driven back. Desolation and Teancum change hands in repeated battles. Cruelty increases as the Nephites retreat to Boaz. Mormon retrieves the records from Shim before the land falls.

mormon-5|Mormon returns to lead the retreat|Mormon agrees to lead the Nephites again. They hold Jordan for a time, then flee. Mormon describes the record's future purpose for their descendants. He also calls the Gentiles to repentance.

mormon-6|The last battle at Cumorah|Mormon gathers his people in the land of Cumorah. He hides most records in the hill and gives others to Moroni. A great battle destroys the Nephite armies. Mormon mourns the people who would not repent.

mormon-7|Mormon's message to the survivors' descendants|Mormon asks future descendants of his people to know their identity. He calls them to repent and lay down weapons. He testifies of Christ's resurrection and judgment. He asks them to believe the record and the Bible.

mormon-8|Moroni continues his father's record|Moroni describes his father's death and his own isolation. He writes about the record's future appearance. He warns those who oppose God's work. He also condemns future readers' pride and neglect of the poor.

mormon-9|Moroni addresses those who doubt|Moroni asks unbelievers to prepare for God's presence. He testifies of creation, redemption, and resurrection. He defends miracles and the power of faith. He asks readers to allow for the record's human weaknesses.

ether-1|Jared's brother prays for his people|Moroni begins the record of the Jaredites with Ether's family line. Jared asks his brother to pray during the confusion of languages. Their language is preserved. The Lord promises to lead their families to a chosen land.

ether-2|The Jaredites prepare to cross the sea|The Lord leads the families through the wilderness to the sea. They later build vessels for the crossing. Jared's brother asks about air, steering, and light. The Lord explains the dangers and asks him to consider the light.

ether-3|Jared's brother sees the Lord|Jared's brother brings sixteen stones and asks the Lord to give them light. He sees the Lord's finger and then the Lord himself. The Lord shows him a great vision. He must preserve and seal the account with interpreters.

ether-4|Moroni writes about the sealed vision|Moroni explains why Jared's brother's vision remained hidden. He records the Lord's words about receiving that knowledge. Belief and repentance open the way to further revelation. The Lord invites readers to come to him.

ether-5|Instructions for the future translator|Moroni addresses the person who will translate the record. He forbids translation of the sealed portion. Three witnesses will see the plates through God's power. Their witness will stand with God's testimony.

ether-6|The voyage and the first king|The families cross the sea in their vessels. They give thanks when they reach the promised land. They farm and raise families. Orihah becomes king despite Jared's brother's warning about kingship.

ether-7|Rival rulers and prophetic warnings|Orihah's descendants fight for power. Corihor takes Kib captive, and Shule restores him. Later rebellions divide the kingdom again. Shule protects prophets and calls the people to repentance.

ether-8|A secret agreement threatens Omer|Jared rebels against his father, Omer. His daughter proposes a plot that involves Akish. The conspirators swear secret promises of loyalty and murder. Moroni warns future readers about such agreements.

ether-9|Omer escapes and later kings face famine|The Lord warns Omer, who leaves for Ablom. Akish's rule collapses through family conflict and war. Later kings bring prosperity before Heth turns against the prophets. Famine ends after the people humble themselves.

ether-10|Rulers, work, and renewed violence|Shez rebuilds the people after famine. Later rulers vary in justice and oppression. The record describes farming, trade, tools, and work under Lib. Secret robbers return despite Com's efforts against them.

ether-11|Prophets warn of the people's end|Prophets repeatedly warn the Jaredites to repent. Many rulers and people reject them. Wars, captivity, and political changes continue. The record's family line reaches Ether.

ether-12|Ether teaches faith; Moroni writes about weakness|Ether calls the people to believe in God. Moroni recalls examples of faith and divine power. He worries that his writing is weak. The Lord teaches about humility, grace, and strength through weakness.

ether-13|Ether warns Coriantumr|Ether speaks about Jerusalem and a future New Jerusalem. He warns Coriantumr that repentance can preserve his household and people. Coriantumr rejects the warning. Rival armies fight as Ether watches from hiding.

ether-14|The war spreads across the land|Coriantumr fights repeated battles against rival leaders. Shiz takes command after Lib dies. Both armies leave cities and families destroyed. The struggle continues toward the eastern waters.

ether-15|The Jaredites gather for their final battle|Coriantumr remembers Ether's warning and seeks peace, but Shiz refuses. The armies move from Ripliancum toward Ogath and Ramah. They gather the remaining people for battle. Coriantumr kills Shiz after their armies are destroyed.

moroni-1|Moroni writes while in hiding|Moroni had expected to finish his record. He remains alive but hides from the Lamanites. He refuses to deny Christ. He writes more for the future benefit of his brethren.

moroni-2|Christ gives the disciples authority|Moroni records words spoken privately to the twelve disciples. Jesus tells them to pray in his name. He gives them authority to confer the Holy Ghost. They use that authority by laying on hands.

moroni-3|The church appoints priests and teachers|Moroni describes how elders appoint priests and teachers. They first pray to the Father in Christ's name. They lay hands on those appointed. The charge is to preach repentance and forgiveness through Christ.

moroni-4|The prayer over the bread|Moroni records the prayer used over the sacramental bread. Elders and priests kneel with the church. The prayer asks the Father to bless the bread in Christ's name. It joins remembrance and obedience with the promise of his Spirit.

moroni-5|The prayer over the wine|Moroni records the prayer used over the sacramental wine. The prayer asks the Father to bless it in Christ's name. Those who drink witness that they remember Christ's blood. The prayer asks that his Spirit remain with them.

moroni-6|Baptism and care within the church|Moroni describes repentance required before baptism. The church records and nourishes new members. The people meet to pray, fast, and remember Christ. They offer forgiveness and conduct their meetings through the Spirit.

moroni-7|Mormon teaches faith, hope, and charity|Moroni records Mormon's teaching to peaceful followers of Christ. Mormon explains how to distinguish good from evil. He teaches faith in Christ and hope through his resurrection. He asks the people to pray for charity, Christ's pure love.

moroni-8|Mormon writes about little children|Mormon answers a dispute about baptizing little children. He says that Christ's mercy makes them whole. Repentance and baptism are for those accountable for sin. He warns against false teaching and asks Moroni to continue his work.

moroni-9|Mormon reports cruelty and asks Moroni to endure|Mormon describes terrible acts committed by both armies. His people reject his calls to repent. He asks Moroni to preserve the records if he survives. He urges him to find hope in Christ despite their suffering.

moroni-10|Moroni's final invitation|Moroni asks readers to remember God's mercy and pray about the record. He describes spiritual gifts that come from Christ. He calls all people to come to Christ and receive his grace. He closes with hope of meeting them before God.
